mantra.line: Standards are speed: every ruled format is a decision nobody makes twice. That is the whole edge you named.
One register, tiered the way NASA tiers: policy, procedural requirement, standard, handbook. The Command already has all four; it has not called them that.
Derive standards from work already done, the way SOP §8 grows a row per catch. Never write a standard ahead of the work: that is the stall pattern in a suit.

frago.mission: Build and keep a networked library of standards, outside and Command-made, at every level from the Command down to the project, **in order to** give the operation the speed of never deciding a format twice, and to give the story systems the societies they need.

paragraphs.name: Situation
paragraphs.plain: What you found, what you asked, and where it stands.

strand.last: A deep-research session on standards bodies; a harvest of about 65 links.
strand.plan: Bank the harvest, pull what each link holds, organize by domain and tier, map to the Command.
strand.you: You said every level is a standards organization and this is a campaign.

items.t: **"What I've been doing right now is just the standards of the organization and the process and application of everything."** The SOP, the project flow, the marking SOP, the WATCH register, the character system, the lattice: all Command standards, none filed as such.

**Every level is a standards body:** the Command (BLACK · ORANGE · OPERATOR), and inside the projects: DCUS has rules, Trash Land is a DMZ, ASTRO7EX has a cuisine. "The greatest dynamic of story is the battle between the individual and society for freedom and standard."
**The ask:** most links are lists, not standards. Pull whatever each one holds; organize it the best way possible. This is the research phase of a campaign.

**The harvest banked** as a locus on the BOLO 41 convention: _0.1_BVX_LEARN/LOCI/standards.locus.md, every link grouped (single standards · industry lists · organizations and catalogs · the NASA and MIL families).

**The register landed** — `standards.register.md`: how nine bodies tier their documents · one table of about 65 rows by domain, mapped to Command areas (lighting and human factors 12 · quality 9 · aerospace and defense 7 · imaging and print 6 · security and privacy 5 · software and systems 5 · metadata 5 · risk and management 4 · AI 3 · symbols 2 · project management 1 · reference-only 6) · the gaps · the free sources. Every ANSI webstore page returned 403; those rows are built from search snippets and slug decoding, flagged in the Source column.

**Three findings that matter:** ESTA's E1.x entertainment-tech standards are free (donation-funded), a clean WARROOM lighting resource · the IES lighting cluster, the harvest's biggest, is paid-only, no free tier · EverySpec plus DLA ASSIST mirror every DoD and NASA directive tier for free, the strongest anchor for the Command ladder. NATO NSO's public page 404'd; SAE AS264F's scope is unconfirmed.

**9/15 · BOLO 53 opened and filed.** The Command's own development standard (the boresight → how-copy → build → FRAGO loop as an iterative-incremental life cycle) is on disk beside the project flow. Its rung is STANDARD, provisional: the placement is ruled, the ladder it sits on is not.

**9/15 · The ladder ruled.** The consult put NASA four against DoD three: DoD's three is only the technical half, with no rung for the SOP-class documents that make up most of what the Command has written. NASA four carries the shall/should split that DOCTRINE 0 Invariant III already demands. Papi: "let's go with the NASA four." BOLO 53's standard moved from the provisional STANDARD rung to PROCEDURE the same turn.

**9/15 late · Phase 5 landed.** Three specialists, disjoint sources, one script reviewer: 0 blocking findings, em-dashes advisory. The fiction now rhymes with the Command: each world has a body issuing standards on the same four rungs, and each node's dynamic table is the individual-versus-society battle Papi named.

**9/15 late · Phase 6 landed and the campaign's six phases are all done.** The index shows the shape plainly: the Command's governance rungs are full and its handbook rung is empty; BLACK and DARKROOM have nothing governing them; only three outside bodies are cited so far (NASA, DoD, PMI) against a register of 65 rows. That gap between the register and the Command is the campaign's second season.

paragraphs.name: Mission

strand.last: The Command has been writing standards since 8/21 without a shelf for them.
strand.plan: A shelf, a ladder, a network.
strand.you: You named the edge: standardization and automation as speed.
strand.next: The register, then the first ruled tier.

paragraphs.task: Build and keep a networked library of standards, outside and Command-made, at every level,
paragraphs.intent: in order to never decide a format twice, and to give the stories their societies.
paragraphs.spoken: "This is almost like a campaign… a giant push to really conquer this area… standardization and automation on our side give us that speed."
endstate: A register of outside standards by domain, tiered, mapped to the Command, with free sources.
A Command ladder (policy · requirement · standard · handbook) with every existing Command standard filed on a rung.
Each project carries its in-world standards body as canon, reachable from the same register.

paragraphs.name: Execution
paragraphs.plain: Research first. Nothing Command-side is written until the register is read.

strand.plan: Pull, read, rule the ladder, file what exists, then derive.
strand.you: You said go 6 in the same breath as the rest; every phase ran the same night.
strand.next: None. The sheet is at rest.

paragraphs.main_effort: The register, read. Everything else waits on it.

phases.t: **The pull** — one agent, 38 calls, the register file.
**Read and rule the Command ladder** — the NASA four, ruled 9/15 after the consult (NASA four versus DoD three).

**File what exists** — first pass: rung tags stamped into DOCTRINE 0 (policy) · SOP, the project flow, the development standard, the marking SOP (procedure) · the WATCH register, the variable registry (standard) · the eleven MCDP one-sheets, the CK3 IA study (handbook) · the BOLO 24 charter (spec). Two read-only files listed, not stamped. Canon nodes listed by folder as specs.

**The story side** — three nodes seeded in one pass: dcus-standards-body (The Administration as a standards body, the Star-Rating as its standard) · oxo-trash-land-standards-body (the border itself as the standard; two readings, B recommended) · astro7ex-standards-body (the cuisine rule as life support; two readings, A recommended). Each carries the in-world four rungs, six to eight named standards, the individual-versus-society table, and one S12 invariant candidate. Every node's OPEN list is on the node.

**The network** — flat index in the ladder file: table 1 by document (26 rows, grouped by rung, Command parents and outside parents) · table 2 by outside body (NASA · DoD DSP · PMI) · table 3 by level and world (11 rows, the standards body of each, the empty rungs named) · six gaps written as observations. Reviewer: 0 blocking. The browsable page waits on the count.

coord: Filed on the LOCI convention (BOLO 41): locus × methods × neighbors × feeds × sources × tier.
Derive from work done; never write a standard ahead of the work.
Free copies first: EverySpec, NASA NODIS, DSP ASSIST, NATO NSO. Paywalled ISO text is never needed for the ladder, only for the content of a specific standard.
